outgoing.name: Agriculture
outgoing.excerpt: With its vast fertile land resources, Negros Oriental's major industry is agriculture.

outgoing.name: Cattle
outgoing.excerpt: People are also involved in cattle ranches, fish ponds and logging.

outgoing.name: Coconut
outgoing.excerpt: The primary crops are sugarcane, corn, coconut and rice.

outgoing.name: Copper
outgoing.excerpt: There are also mineral deposits like gold, silver and copper.

outgoing.name: English language
outgoing.excerpt: Filipino and English are generally understood, and are used for official, literary, and educational purposes.

outgoing.name: Fishing
outgoing.excerpt: In the coastal area, fishing is the main source of income.

outgoing.name: United States
outgoing.excerpt: In 1901 the Negros Oriental province was reorganized by the United States and a civil government was established with Demetrio Larena as governor.

outgoing.name: World War II
outgoing.excerpt: During World War II, the province was invaded by Japanese forces and many residents were forced to flee to the mountains to escape.
